Rumor has long pointed out that Apple is developing a brand-new iPhone with an all-glass design for next year's 20th anniversary. However, Jefferies analysts believe the device is no longer moving forward.

Wall Street analysts say the major redesign of the 20th anniversary iPhone has been cancelled

Wall Street investment bank Jefferies downgraded Apple's stock rating to "Underperform" today, with analyst Edison Lee pointing out that the possible cancellation of the 20th anniversary iPhone's major redesign is one of the main reasons.

The key to this downgrade lies in the suspected cancellation of Apple's all-glass iPhone. Although reports as early as 2025 indicated the project was under development, and there were rumors it would debut as soon as 2027, Apple has never commented on the speculation. However, the company quietly filed a patent for a "six-sided glass enclosure" back in 2019. Jefferies had previously considered it possible to launch an all-glass iPhone, but Lee believes development work has come to a halt. According to the analyst, supply chain investigations show the project was cancelled due to excessively low yield rates. Lee considers this decision "a major setback in pushing for higher-priced iPhones amid soaring memory costs." If the device were indeed launched in September 2027 to commemorate the iPhone's 20th anniversary, the estimated average retail price would be $2,060 — higher than the average price of any previous model. Lee wrote: "More importantly, we believe the original plan was to extend the all-glass design to future iPhone Pro and Pro Max models, further increasing their average selling price and gross margins." He believes that with memory prices constantly climbing, this was originally a crucial defensive move.

Lee also pointed out that Apple's AI strategy and rising component costs for the iPhone 19 Pro are reasons for the further downgrade of the company's stock rating.

From Lee's report, it is difficult to determine whether the analyst believes the entire redesign has been shelved, or only some design elements.

For example, long-circulating speculation in the market suggests Apple may not be able to completely remove the Dynamic Island cutout next year. Therefore, an "all-glass" screen will not be achievable. However, the rumored four-sided curved design may still be launched.

Regardless, if Apple's plans for the iPhone 20th anniversary design have truly been cancelled, other credible sources should soon confirm it.

What are your thoughts on this report about the iPhone 20th anniversary design? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
